Origin & Botanical Facts
The nectarine is indigenous to Asia, from
where it made its way to Europe and finally
to the Americas.  The name “nectarine”
is thought to be a derivative of the name
of the Greek god Nektar, and the juice
of the fruit has been referred to as the
“drink of the gods.”  The nectarine is a
member of the rose (Rosaceae) family.

Nectarine
Baked nectarine halves can be served with
baked chicken or ham, and they make a
delicious dessert.
Nutrient composition
Nectarines are high in vitamin A (beta-
carotene) and are a good source of vitamin
C.  The pit of the nectarine contains
amygdalin, a compound that is converted
to cyanide in the stomach.  Although not
likely, swallowing an occasional pit acci-
dentally is not harmful.
